newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-BRIVE FLY FLAG FOR FRENCH NATIONAL SIDE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-BRIVE FLY FLAG FOR FRENCH NATIONAL SIDE.

text.p: Brive's European Cup triumph could inspire the French national team to new heights, according to Leicester's former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer.

Brive's scored four excellent tries in their impressive 28-9 victory over their English opponents and Dwyer suggested their united forwards and fast, powerful backs signalled the way ahead for France.
"They are not like a normal French team. They do the easy things very well and sometimes French teams think the easy things are not worth thinking about," said Dwyer.
"This is a team which has kept all the qualities of French rugby and improved some of the things which are not of international standard in the French style."

Brive coach Laurent Seigne played his part by ensuring his team raced on to the field pumped up for a big game and his assistant Pierre Montlaur suggested national coach Jean-Claude Skrela should take note of their performance.
"I noticed he was at the game...I hope he paid attention to what he saw," said Montlaur. "The players now have the reward they justly deserve.
All the Brive backs caught the eye, especially winger Sebastien Carrat who scored two tries, but their forwards were also a compelling unit against one of the most disciplined English club packs.
They posed as many problems in the line-out and Leicester captain Dean Richards rated the encounter alongside some of the most bruising internationals he has played for England.
"It was very high standard for a club game," he said, nursing a scratched eye which forced him off in the second-half.
"The manner of our defeat was a bit of a shock and a jolt, especially for the younger players."
